source.title: Generalized equivalences between subsampling and ridge regularization

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study proves and illustrates that prediction risk for optimally tuned ridge is monotone in the data aspect ratio, refining the claim that more data can hurt and that double descent persists under optimal regularization.
record.gate_note: The study tests risk behavior as data aspect ratio changes, especially for optimally tuned ridge and subsampled ridgeless regression. It does not sweep deep-network size or training epochs. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows; the random-feature and kernel-feature plots concern subsampling–ridge equivalences, not the specified double-descent axes.
record.test_reason: Theorem 6 proves that, under proportional asymptotics, optimally tuned ridge prediction risk increases monotonically in ϕ = p/n. The same holds for the subsample-optimized ridgeless ensemble. This directly answers whether sample-wise non-monotonicity (V3) persists under optimal regularization (V6). It does so by asymptotic proof, not by a deep-network sweep. The proof needs fixed linearized signal and nonlinear energies across ϕ.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors show risk and structural equivalences between subsampling and ridge for general (nonlinear) data. As an indirect consequence, they show optimally tuned ridge risk is monotone increasing in p/n under proportional asymptotics. This settles Nakkiran et al.'s Conjecture 1, provided the linearized SNR is held fixed across aspect ratios. They say this means optimal ridge avoids sample-wise non-monotonicity and mitigates double or multiple descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes ridge and subsampled ridge estimators using proportional-asymptotic risk results and simulations; it does not reproduce a deep-network size or epoch sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The monotonicity result depends on optimal tuning and on assumptions maintaining comparable signal-to-noise levels and finite limiting energies.

fits_no_version.finding: Subsampling and ridge regularization give asymptotically equivalent estimators and generalized risks along linear paths in the (λ, ψ) plane. Empirically this extends to random-feature and kernel ridge models and to CIFAR-10, MNIST and USPS.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subsample ensembling acts as implicit ridge regularization of a data-estimable strength.

record.problems: The monotonicity theorem is asymptotic and conditional on its regularity assumptions. The illustrative figure does not provide numeric risk values in the text, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly test the listed versions. Cited double-descent findings and the random-feature and kernel-feature equivalence plots were not extracted as rows because they do not test the specified model-size, epoch, sample-size-peak, or effective-complexity claims.

record.verdict_notes: Nakkiran et al. (Optimal regularization can mitigate double descent) is not among the listed originals, so verdicts are allowed. The evidence is a proof, with no uncertainty estimates. The monotonicity relies on fixed ρ² and σ² across ϕ; without that, risk comparisons across ϕ are not of equal hardness. The equivalence experiments (Figures 1–3, 5–7, F8) are the study's own method validations, not double-descent measurements, and are correctly excluded as rows.

The study addresses monotonicity under optimal ridge tuning, but does not test whether label noise or variance drives peaks, whether peaks split, or other regularization choices.

rows.subject: optimal full-ensemble ridgeless regression
rows.size_stated: n, p, k → ∞; p/n → ϕ and p/k → ψ
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed optimal prediction risk as the data aspect ratio ϕ varies, minimizing over subsample aspect ratio ψ ≥ ϕ.

conditions.value: Theorem 1 conditions and Assumptions 3–4; fixed limiting linearized and nonlinearized energies
optimal prediction risk minψ≥ϕ R(0; ϕ, ψ)

rows.note: Since ϕ = p/n, the stated direction means risk decreases as sample size increases with feature dimension fixed. The result is asymptotic and assumes comparable regression hardness across problems.
rows.check: Subsampling acts as implicit regularization equivalent to ridge, so the subsample-optimized ensemble also bears on V6. The risk is monotone in p/n, so no sample-wise hump appears. Ordinary improvement with more data is not the opposite of V3's effect, so 'absent' fits better than 'reversed'. This is proof-based with no numeric values.

rows.subject: optimal ridge predictor
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed optimal prediction risk as the data aspect ratio ϕ varies, minimizing over ridge penalty λ ≥ 0.

conditions.value: Theorem 1 conditions and Assumptions 3–4; fixed limiting linearized and nonlinearized energies
optimal prediction risk minλ≥0 R(λ; ϕ, ϕ)

rows.note: The authors say this monotonicity mitigates double- or multiple-descent behavior for optimally tuned ridge. As ϕ = p/n, the risk direction is opposite to more data raising risk.
rows.check: For V3, the effect is absent rather than reversed: with optimal λ, more samples never raise risk. For V6 the version's prediction is borne out (the peak vanishes under optimal tuning), but the row's state is recorded relative to the peak. It holds only under Assumptions 3–4, which keep the SNR fixed across ϕ.
